questions.question: The effective date of the new 'healthy' claim rule was delayed. Did the compliance deadline change?
We make a strawberry frosting containing FD&C Red No. 3. When exactly must we stop using it, and is product already on shelves illegal after that date?
must_not_contain: regardless of when it was manufactured
questions.note:
SME-seat ruling 2026-08-15, with sources. REWRITTEN, not patched. The previous accept group was ["not adulterated", "may remain", "manufactured before"] and had one proven defect and one investigation error behind it.

THE DEFECT: "manufactured before" MATCHED THE NEGATION OF THE INTENDED ANSWER. Measured, not theorised — over ten live runs the question passed about 1 in 4, and every passing run matched inside this sentence: "The sources do not provide an explicit FDA enforcement-discretion statement or transition period for products manufactured before the effective date but still in commerce after it." That is an answer saying it CANNOT confirm the allowance, scoring as though it had confirmed it. Failing runs said the same thing as "regardless of when it was manufactured" and scored zero. The check was tracking phrasing in both directions — the fourth defect the q07 ruling named, reproduced here. The token is removed and cannot come back.

THE INVESTIGATION ERROR, recorded because it nearly cost the question: it was first reported as requiring an answer the corpus cannot support, on a corpus scan showing zero hits for "not adulterated", "may remain", "manufactured before", "manufactured prior", "existing stocks" and "sell-through". That scan searched for the QUESTION's phrasings, not the SOURCE's. The proposition is squarely citable and always was. 90 FR 4628 (doc 2025-00830), section VI. Conclusion, chunk #0021: "In accordance with 21 CFR 80.32(h), all certificates for existing batches and portions of batches of FD&C Red No. 3 will cease to be effective for use in food on the effective date for the removal of 74.303 ... Use of FD&C Red No. 3 after its certificate ceases to be effective will result in such food or ingested drugs being adulterated. When FD&C Red No. 3 has been used in food or ingested drugs while its certificate is still effective, such food or ingested drugs will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use of such color additive." Falsifiable by reading that chunk, or by FR full-text search for "will not be regarded as adulterated by reason of the use".

So the accept tokens now match the SOURCE's language rather than a paraphrase of it, and the second group requires the CERTIFICATION mechanism the order actually turns on — 21 CFR 80.32(h), certificates ceasing to be effective — because an answer that reaches the right conclusion without it is reasoning from somewhere other than the document.

WHY THE QUESTION WAS FAILING was neither of the above: the answer layer truncated retrieved passages at 1200 characters, a constant inherited from the reranker where it is correct for RANKING. Chunk 2025-00830#0021 is 1891 characters and the decisive sentence starts at 1811, so retrieval ranked the answer SECOND and the verdict node then sliced it off and reported that its sources were silent. Fixed by bounding passages at the chunker's own CHUNK_MAX_CHARS; a regression test pins it. After the fix the question passes 3/3 with the answer quoting the sentence above.

must_not_contain is assertion-shaped and bans the WRONG CONCLUSION, not vocabulary: "adulterated regardless of when" and "regardless of when it was manufactured" are the exact form the pre-fix answers took. "recall required" and "January 18, 2028 for food" are retained from the original — the drug date is 74.1303's and applying it to food is the other half of this trap.

questions.question: Our fruit-flavored cocktail mixer contains Red No. 3 and its formula is on file with another federal agency. When must we stop using Red No. 3, and is there anything else we are obliged to do that you cannot confirm from your sources?
questions.note: SME-seat ruling 2026-08-12, with sources. REPLACES a version that was a FALSE PASS — worse than a false fail, because it is invisible. It asked '(TTB-approved formula) ... what do we need to do beyond reformulating?' and accepted must_contain_any [['TTB','formula approval','new formula']] while requiring a citation to 90 FR 4628 or 21 CFR 74.303. Two defects. (1) The token 'TTB' was in the question STEM, so echoing the stem scored correct and the assertion proved nothing. (2) It rewarded attaching a Red No. 3 citation to a TTB proposition that document does not support: verified by direct read of the full corpus at 985 chunks — 2025-00830 contains NO mention of TTB, alcohol, or formula approval, and there is no TTB source document anywhere in the corpus (corroborates milestones/M00b/README.md finding 2, which drafted a tightening that was never applied). The corrected question splits what IS citable from what is not, which is the property this product lives on. Citable: the mixer is a food, so the removal of 21 CFR 74.303 by 90 FR 4628 (doc 2025-00830, DATES: 'This order is effective January 15, 2027, except for amendatory instruction 4, which is effective January 18, 2028') ends the permitted use on 2027-01-15. NOT citable: any obligation owed to the other agency — so the answer must SAY it cannot confirm that from its sources rather than assert it. The agency name is removed from the stem so the answer cannot be echoed; must_not_contain is narrow and assertion-shaped ('TTB requires') rather than banning the token, because naming TTB as an open question is CORRECT behaviour and only asserting its requirements as established is wrong. Do not re-add a TTB citation to must_cite_any unless a TTB source document enters the corpus — that is a PM-seat scope decision, not an SME one.

questions.question: HHS asked manufacturers to phase out Red No. 3 sooner than 2027. Is that binding on us?
must_not_contain: must comply with the HHS date
legally required to phase out early

questions.question: What are the two main criteria a food must meet to use the 'healthy' claim under the updated rule?
Which CFR section governs the 'healthy' implied nutrient content claim?

We have $8M in annual food sales and we make a granola bar labeled 'healthy'. Some labeling rules give smaller manufacturers an extra year to comply. What is our compliance date for the 'healthy' rule?
questions.note: SME-seat ruling 2026-08-12, with sources. REPLACES a version that required the fabricated extension and forbade the correct answer: must_contain_any was ['four','additional year','extra year','smaller'] and must_not_contain was ['same deadline as large manufacturers']. Three defects. (1) It demanded a small-business extension the rule does not contain. FDA expressly DECLINED one: 2024-29957#0303, Response 135 under 'J. Effective and Compliance Dates' — 'we do not have information that would enable us to determine whether all or merely some small businesses need additional time'. Falsify via FR full-text search for 'merely some small businesses need additional time' -> 1 hit, this rule. (2) must_not_contain forbade a true statement, punishing vocabulary rather than error. (3) It could not distinguish true from false answers in EITHER direction, because 'no extra time for smaller manufacturers' matched the accept token 'smaller' while 'the date is uniform' did not match anything. It failed 0/3 at the M00b control (7f012b8-naive-full.json, reason: none of ['four','additional year','extra year','smaller'] present) and has never passed at any recorded commit. Do not restore it. The $10M/extra-year tier is REAL in FDA labeling but belongs to other rules — Nutrition Facts 81 FR 33742, extension 83 FR 19619, and the Front-of-Package proposed rule 90 FR 5426 — so the bait now sits in the question stem and passing requires contradicting the premise. Verified against the live corpus at 985 chunks: '$10 million' and 'annual food sales' both return ZERO hits. must_not_contain is deliberately just ['2029'] and NOT the fabrication tokens: a correct answer may legitimately say 'FDA considered and declined an additional 2 years', and forbidding 'additional year' would punish it — the same defect this correction removes. The scorer is substring-only (run_evals.py check()) and cannot express 'asserts X' versus 'mentions X'; the guard here is the required right date plus required uniformity language, which a fabricated answer fails twice over. Applicability under this rule turns on CONDUCT (does the label bear a 'healthy' claim), never company size. OPEN ITEM FOR THE PM SEAT, created by this correction: adding the 'trap' tag here makes the tag-selected trap set (now q01-q04 plus q07) diverge from SPEC/03's Done-when, which names 'q01-q04 (trap questions)' by ID, and from SPEC/00b line 22 which does the same. run_evals.py selects by TAG (--subset), so 'make evals --subset trap' and 'q01-q04' are no longer the same five questions. The tag is kept deliberately — CLAUDE.md's presumption protects trap questions from later weakening, and this one now baits a plausible wrong answer in its stem, so it is a trap in substance. But SPEC/03's exit criterion must be reworded to say 'the trap subset' rather than an ID range, or q07 explicitly excluded. Engineering must not pick one silently: the tag reading is STRICTER, and quietly tightening a milestone's exit criterion is not engineering's call.

questions.question: List publication, effective, and compliance dates for the Red No. 3 revocation as they apply to food.
questions.note: SME correction 2026-08-08. This asked for the publication date but accepted 'January 15, 2025', which is FDA's ANNOUNCEMENT date. 90 FR 4628 published 2025-01-16, and the string 'January 15, 2025' appears nowhere in the document — so the old assertion failed a correct, citable answer and passed an uncitable one. It is also the likeliest cause of q08 being the only question that flapped in the M00b baseline (1/3); see milestones/M00b. Do not 'correct' this back. The order states EFFECTIVE dates and sets no compliance date at all (ADR-0006), so an answer that says so is right; must_contain_any below accepts either that observation or a derived deadline, but must_not_contain forbids asserting a compliance date the order does not set.
must_contain_any: does not set a compliance date
